I have a SIG P229 for awhile. Primarily due to it not having a safety, I have opted to carry in Condition 3.

Thinking back to every street fight I've ever been in, they all start with a sucker punch. I have been watching some CC Defense surveillance footage and racking the slide requires both hands or +5 to my ninja stat. I've always ended up needing at least one arm to defend myself. Of course this now puts me in the position that if I am knocked out/dazed and they get my weapon, they don't need to rack it. Decisions decisions.

Wondering your thoughts on this? Next year I will probably do some research now that I am getting into shooting again and go for my CCW with something with a safety that I can operate one handed easily.
Has this sub had the "Israeli Carry" debate?
I carry my 1911 and my p938 with one in the chamber. In fact, I always keep all of my guns loaded with one in the pipe.

If it's carried concealed,

  • You are only ever drawing it if you are ready to shoot, at that point chambering (and a safety) are in your way
  • attackers will should not be aware of your weapon even if they jump you-the sucker punch will be a punch, not a "sucker gun grab"
  • In the videos you watched, how many people had both hands available to draw their gun? How many people had time to rack it? Would you bet your life that you always will?
  • In the videos you watched, how many concealed carriers had their weapon taken after being jumped?

I agree that one-handed operation is preferable.

The question of weapon retention is not really addressed by adding a safety; its a matter of technique. A good class is ideal but there are dozens of youtube videos to learn from too.

Your fear of losing your weapon to an attacker who is motivated to kill you is arguably best addressed by being prepared to quickly and decisively stop the attacker who is motivated to kill you, rather than weakening your response in hopes it might slow him down a little. Be ready to shoot instantly - let him be the guy who has to worry about your gun.

Your P229 is a fine pistol. The long double action pull for the first shot makes it perfectly safe for loaded-chamber carry and ideal for a quick, gross-motor-skill first shot without fussing with any added levers. Learn to draw and fire from a retention position and practice - dry fire is your friend - until the movements are natural and instinctive. It will not render you invulnerable from harm, but it can make you as invulnerable as you can be.

You might consider a 'retention holster'. The gun is not coming out unless you press the magic lever:

http://www.safariland.com/products/holste

Carrying with no safety and loaded is only dangerous if you are poorly trained. There is no reason to carry any other way, just remember basic safety rules like, no finger on trigger until ready to shoot, and never point a gun at something you don't want to destroy.

It's called the Israeli carry because back in the day when Israel was a new country it mostly had a mix of hand-me-down arms and nothing was really standardized. It's not like they were all revolvers or 1911s or M9s where you can just tell everyone to carry a specific way. The Israeli carry was an attempt to get everyone on the same page as far as carrying is concerned. It was out of necessity to standardize it was developed not necessarily because it was the best method to carry.

Having said that I think what's most important is you consistently carry and in a matter you're most comfortable with and constantly be training. Even if you're only comfortable carrying a 22 without a round chambered today, with growing confidence and skill I'm certain anyone will eventually work their way up to condition 1 or 0 with something bigger.
